Studies5 have suggested that the ventricular arrhythmias are due to terfenadine itself rather than its active metabolite fexofenadine (p.579). Terfenadine has been shown to inhibit cardiac potassium channels, which results in prolongation of the QT interval, a risk factor for developing arrhythmias, while the non-sedating anti- histamines cetirizine, fexofenadine, and loratadine have had no demonstrable effect5,6 (see also p.562). 1. No adverse effects have been observed in breast-fed infants whose mothers were receiving terfenadine, and the American Academy of Pediatrics1 considers that it is therefore usually compatible with breast feeding.
